title: Wildlife Documentary Director Studio
description: The user directs a wildlife documentary scene where a Robot cinematographer operates an AntiqueCamera to film a Fox performing various animations. Users control the Fox's animation clips, position the AntiqueCamera on a dolly track around the scene, adjust the Robot's filming pose, set playback speed, toggle a picture-in-picture camera preview, and trigger a final cinematic slow-motion replay sequence.
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive wildlife documentary director studio.

SCENE SETUP: Load Fox.glb at center on a grassy green circular ground plane (radius 8). Load robot.glb scaled to 1.2 standing behind AntiqueCamera.glb, both positioned on a visible curved dolly track (a torus segment ring, radius 5, around the Fox). Add warm directional light simulating golden-hour sun, soft ambient light, and a subtle spotlight on the Fox. Use a sky-blue background. Place the main perspective camera at an elevated 3/4 angle with OrbitControls.

ANIMATION SYSTEM: Extract all AnimationClips from Fox.glb (Survey, Walk, Run). Use THREE.AnimationMixer to manage them. The Robot should have a subtle idle bobbing animation via code (sinusoidal Y oscillation).

INTERACTIONS (6-10 steps with validation):
1. ANIMATION SELECT: A dropdown selects Fox animation clips (Survey/Walk/Run). Validate clip exists before playing. Crossfade between clips over 0.5s.
2. PLAYBACK SPEED: A slider (0.1 to 3.0, step 0.1, default 1.0) controls Fox animation timeScale. Validate range before applying.
3. DOLLY POSITION: A slider (0 to 360 degrees, step 1) rotates the Robot+AntiqueCamera group along the dolly track around the Fox. The camera model must always lookAt the Fox. Validate angle is numeric and in range.
4. ROBOT HEIGHT: A slider (0.5 to 2.5, default 1.2) adjusts Robot Y scale to simulate crouching or standing tall. Validate min/max.
5. PIP TOGGLE: A checkbox enables a picture-in-picture viewport (small inset renderer in bottom-right corner, 250x180px) rendering from a secondary camera positioned at the AntiqueCamera model's world position, looking at the Fox. Validate PIP camera exists before rendering.
6. RECORD REPLAY: A button labeled 'Cinematic Replay' triggers a 5-second automated sequence: dolly smoothly sweeps 180 degrees, Fox animation switches to Run at timeScale 0.3 (slow-motion), and a vignette CSS overlay fades in. Validate replay is not already running before starting. Disable controls during replay and re-enable after.

UI: Use a styled fixed panel (top-left, semi-transparent dark background, white text) containing all controls. Show current dolly angle and playback speed as live readouts. All sliders must show their current numeric value.
